newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb before Algeria vote kills one, wounds 13.
newsitem.headline: Bomb before Algeria vote kills one, wounds 13.

text.p: A bomb explosion on Monday at a bus shelter killed one man and wounded 13 other people in a small town near Algiers, the security forces said.

A statement carried by the official APS news agency said six of the people were "badly wounded" when the bomb exploded near the hospital in Berrouaghia, 70 km (45 miles) south of Algiers. It did not say who was responsible.

The explosion, which APS initially said happened last Saturday, came as Algerians prepare to vote on constitutional changes that would bar Moslem fundamentalists from seeking power. The Armed Islamic Group, which wants to disrupt the referendum, warned people this week not to vote.
Although the government insists the poll will be held in "full freedom and tranquility," violence has continued unabated.
Algerian newspapers dubbed this the "Month of all horrors". More than 120 people have been killed in the past six weeks, according to independent sources in Algiers.

A car bomb killed five people and wounded 19 on Sunday in the central garrison town of Blida, newspapers said on Monday. Security forces killed nine guerrillas in two operations in the previous 24 hours near Algiers, newspapers also reported.
Algerian residents report tightened security to pre-empt Moslem guerrilla attacks, with more soldiers and patrols around main cities.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
